title: Magna Hungaria
fact_summary: The name for an area in the Volga-Ural region where Hungarians who had not migrated west were reported in the 13th century.

claims.text: Hungarians who remained in the Volga-Ural region were reported in the middle of the 13th century; archaeologists associate their heritage with the Chiyalik culture, in the area known as Magna Hungaria.

held_by.who: Szeifert et al. (2022), summarising earlier research

claims.certainty_reason: A summary in one tier B study. The 13th-century report has not been opened yet.

claims.text: A 2025 genetic study reports that a late medieval group of the Chiyalik culture on the lower Kama stayed within the same cluster of relatives as the early Hungarians, with radiocarbon dates in the late 14th century.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: “We assume that the Low Kama region near the Belaya-Kama confluence was the area that was called Magna Hungaria by Friar Julian in the 13th century.”
claims.certainty_reason: The authors word this as an assumption. Friar Julian's report, which they cite, has not been read.

claims.text: Place-names suggest Hungarian-speaking groups lived there “until the 16th century”.
claims.certainty_reason: Rests on place-name studies the authors cite, which have not been opened.

open_questions.text: A 2025 study names Friar Julian as the 13th-century reporter. What exactly did he write, and where does his report survive? It has not been read yet.

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
